Merge loop/ci-audit: The GitHub Action gains an opt-in audit mode that runs the audit agent through Claude Code in CI and reports its findings, never pushing (ADR 0005, I2).

Merge loop/adr-audit-fixes: Fix what the first audit of kmctl's own decision log found: the briefing names its skills (ADR 0002), the records drop two fields no ADR allows (I4), and seven records gain their Consequences.

Merge loop/ci-audit-hardening: The audit mode keeps the GitHub token away from the model, and a failed issue lookup fails the step instead of opening a second issue (ci-audit review findings f3 and f4).

Merge loop/kmctl-docs: kmctl gets the docs its own rules ask for: a README with the real install line, user pages in docs/ by Diataxis type written with the write-docs skill, and an architecture page in .okf/.

Merge loop/plugin-install-known-marketplace: kmctl plugin install adds the okf marketplace from the source the operator's user or managed settings already list, instead of failing when that source differs from scaccogatto/okf-skills.

Merge loop/audit-any-provider: The CI audit runs Hermes Agent against any OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenAI, Ollama, Bifrost, OpenRouter and others) instead of Claude Code with an Anthropic key, and the shipped workflow spells out every command it runs.

Merge loop/audit-hermes-hardening: The Hermes audit runs once per batch of at most ten concepts, so no prompt reaches Linux's 128 KiB argument limit, and it clears HERMES_MANAGED_DIR so no managed config overrides its own (audit-any-provider review findings f2 and f3).

Merge loop/init-seeds-the-habit: kmctl init sets a repository up so an agent keeps its knowledge: it writes the knowledge rules as files, adds a kmctl block to CLAUDE.md, records the first decision (keep knowledge in OKF), and tells the agent what to write next.

Merge loop/init-claude-md-always: kmctl init writes CLAUDE.md with the kmctl block whenever it is missing, even when AGENTS.md exists, as the operator asked, and never writes through a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md symlink that is dangling or points outside the repository.

Merge loop/new-concept-freshness: kmctl new takes --stale-after and repeatable --source, so the concepts agents write carry the two fields kmctl review due already reads, and the kmctl block tells agents to use them.
Add the integration gate for network-tests-retry

Merge loop/network-tests-retry: The plugin install tests that reach GitHub become an integration tier, left out of the default pytest run as the python-testing rule asks, run at every stamp by a gate of their own, and retried on a network error only.

Merge loop/schema-verbs: A kmctl schema command group prints the expected shape of each kind of document kmctl knows (concepts, bundle files, architecture pages, docs pages): its front matter as JSON Schema and its body sections, built from kmctl's own code so it cannot drift.

Merge loop/plugin-error-keeps-cause: When a claude plugin command fails, kmctl's error names the line that says why (a git fatal or error line, such as Could not resolve host) instead of only claude's last stderr line, so an offline install no longer reads as an access-rights problem.

Merge loop/release-flow: kmctl gets a hand-run release workflow that opens a version pull request and a tag workflow that, when it lands, tags main and publishes a GitHub Release with the wheel, sdist and SHA256SUMS, with the plugin manifest as the one version source; GitHub Releases only, no PyPI.
Measure help text without colour codes in tests
body:
On GitHub Actions typer forces a colour terminal, so --help output carries
ANSI codes. The 80-column check counted them as width and the freshness
check found option names split by them; both failed in CI only. They now
strip the codes first, through plain() in conftest.

subject: agent-audit: claims, checks, judge, and a review page with feedback
body:
kmctl audit extracts a bundle's claims through an agent (claims todo,
submit, list), turns them into checks kmctl reruns with no model (checks
todo, try, submit, run, list), and asks an optional decision model for a
second look (judge). A guard hook holds the agents to kmctl audit commands,
and answers follow a claim when re-extraction rewords it (ADR 0036 to 0040).

kmctl audit ui serves a page on 127.0.0.1 where a person gives a claim or
its check a thumbs up or down and a note, says whether the claim holds, and
asks for a second opinion. Feedback is appended to .kmctl/audit.sqlite; a
thumbs down, or a verdict the check contradicts, sends the work back to the
agent with the next todo, and liked answers become examples (ADR 0041).

Also: the audit UI and mixed-claims prototypes, the extract-claims and
write-checks skills and their agents, docs for every new verb, and the
devcontainer setup. The repository's own apm.yml drops the agent-creator,
rule-creator and generate-art skills and adds Anthropic's frontend-design
skill, pinned to 2c5958ec, with APM 0.35's lock and the manifest tests
updated to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: audit: code view, code coverage, clearer check results, measured costs
body:
Each check step now records the lines it matched, and kmctl audit coverage
and a new code view in kmctl audit ui count a line of code as covered when a
stored check matched it on its last run (ADR 0042). Runs on files that changed
since are stale and not counted; a deleted file is left out. The page links
claims and code both ways, shows a block strip per file, and says plainly
whether each check holds, step by step, and why one was not measured.

Also: the drifts the audit found in the overview and the pipeline doc are
fixed, and .okf/prototypes/token-costs measures what the audit agents cost
from 141 real runs (extraction $0.0068 a section, check writing $0.0081 a
claim on Claude Haiku 5.5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: audit ui: a View code button on each check
body:
Each check card opens the lines its check matched, with three lines of
context, or for a check that tests whole files, each file it read. It
warns when a file changed since the check ran. The file endpoint now
serves any tracked text file a check may read, and refuses binary files
and links that lead out of the repository.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: audit: honest second opinions, others' feedback apart, two overview drifts
body:
- The page fills its vote, verdict and note only from your own feedback;
  someone else's shows read-only with who gave it, and their open thumbs
  down stays unless you thumb it yourself. A verdict names who gave it.
- A link answer carries each level's probability; the page calls it a
  guess and says the model is unsure when no level reaches 70%. Levels
  outside 0 to 3 are refused rather than misread.
- The link question counts finding the exact text or value a claim
  describes as testing the claim, and ignores parts no file could show.
- overview: what kmctl audit ui writes (the cache table, and a removed
  section's rows), and how kinds.py relates to ALLOWED_FIELDS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: prototypes: measure how the reworded link question moved its answers
body:
Re-judging 679 checks: "the claim itself" rose from 198 to 328 and the
median score from 0.70 to 0.76, wording checks from 0.75 to 0.84.
compare.py reruns the numbers from the store. Also logs the overview
drift fixes that a29ddf1e left out of log.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Merge loop/kmaudit-package: Move the audit out of kmctl into its own package, kmaudit, that runs without kmctl.
Merge loop/kmaudit-namespaces: kmaudit audits any folder of markdown docs, each folder in its own store, listed by kmaudit namespaces.
Merge loop/kmaudit-briefing: kmaudit briefing prints each namespace's audit state in a few lines, read-only, for a session-start hook.
Merge loop/kmaudit-mcp: kmaudit mcp starts a stdio MCP server whose tools are kmaudit's verbs, so any MCP harness can drive the audit.
Merge loop/kmctl-to-packages: Move kmctl into packages/kmctl and make the root a uv virtual workspace, with install lines, pins and the release build following it.
Merge loop/ci-per-package: Split the CI workflow into one test job per package, named CI, while main's required checks and the loop's gates keep covering both packages.
Merge loop/release-per-package: Release kmctl or kmaudit from one Release run, each with its own version source, tag family and path-filtered notes committed in the version pull request.

Merge loop/release-notes-hermes: The manual Release run has Hermes rewrite the deterministic notes draft into user-facing notes, and a cleaning script keeps the rewrite only when it passes checks, else the draft stands.

Merge loop/release-skill: A repo-local release skill that takes the package name and walks the dry run, the real run, the notes review in the version pull request and the check of the published notes.
Merge loop/release-per-package-reviewer-f1: Deferred hardening from release-per-package, reviewer finding f1 in review round 1.
Merge loop/kmaudit-namespaces-nested-store: kmaudit namespaces and briefing open a nested namespace's store, whose file name holds %2F, instead of failing with unable to open database file.

Merge loop/root-release-cutoff: v0.12.2 was built from the repository root, so the subdirectory cutoff moves from v0.12.1 to v0.12.2, and release.py set writes the fragment only for releases after it.
Merge loop/release-notes-hermes-reviewer-f2: Deferred hardening from release-notes-hermes, reviewer finding f2 in review round 1.

Merge loop/release-notes-owned-paths: kmctl's release notes leave out commits that touch only paths no package ships (.loop/, .okf/, .claude/, uv.lock), and release-tag's late-commit check uses the same rule from one place.
Merge loop/apm-per-package: Each package keeps its APM package and its version in its own folder, packages/kmctl/apm and packages/kmaudit/apm, so kmaudit's version stops living in a VERSION file.
Merge loop/kmaudit-install-hints-pinned: A kmaudit release pins every install hint kmaudit prints or documents, not only the README line.
Merge loop/kmaudit-skills-mcp: kmaudit's skills and agents move into kmaudit's own APM package and call its MCP tools instead of its CLI, and the package declares the kmaudit MCP server.
Merge loop/kmaudit-cli-slim: kmaudit's CLI keeps only mcp, ui, the list commands and briefing; the verbs live on as MCP tools.

Merge loop/readmes-per-package: The root README becomes a short map to the two package READMEs and docs/, kmctl's README carries its install and use, and kmaudit's command reference moves into the root docs/.
Merge loop/upgrade-from-v0-12-docs: kmctl's README and the APM how-to give the full path from v0.12.x to a later release, CLI first, and point auditing at kmaudit.
Merge loop/kmaudit-tests-git-identity: kmaudit's test git helper commits with its own identity, so the kmaudit CI job passes on a runner with no git config.
